purpose: Resolve the remaining claim-level evidence holds across the complete Book while preserving fail-closed publication rules and correcting stale ledger summary counts without rewriting historical claim records.

auditCorrections.reason: The stored summary does not match the 33 individual claim conclusions. The individual claim records are treated as authoritative; this audit supersedes only the summary counts.

newEvidence.title: How to Prevent and Troubleshoot Short Shots
newEvidence.scope: States that insufficient available injection pressure or an injection-pressure limit set too low can make a filling process pressure-limited so constant commanded velocity is not maintained as resistance changes. Used as process-control evidence, not as a universal pressure-setting source.

newEvidence.title: SE-EV-S technical data
newEvidence.scope: Documents machine-specific screw-position display, maximum/minimum cushion monitoring, filling-pressure monitoring and V/P switchover functions. Supports use of screw position/cushion as controller-specific process signals, not a universal cushion target.

newEvidence.title: Tips for process optimization in injection molding
newEvidence.scope: Treats melt-cushion fluctuation as a monitored process signal and links variation to settings and screw condition. Does not define a universal cushion value.

newEvidence.title: Venting Solutions
newEvidence.scope: Describes application-specific venting methods, placement and engineered components and identifies short-shot studies as a way to locate critical venting areas. Does not establish one universal vent geometry.

newEvidence.title: Sintered Vents FAQ
newEvidence.scope: States that vent selection and performance vary with resin grade/viscosity and refers users to product installation specifications and resin suppliers for application-specific limits.

newEvidence.title: Predictive maintenance and mold monitoring in injection molding
newEvidence.scope: Explains that controlled mould heat removal depends on the temperature-control medium/system and that in-mould temperature sensing can detect restricted flow or heat-transfer malfunctions. Supports measurement-based cooling diagnosis rather than treating a controller setpoint as proof of mould thermal state.

newEvidence.title: Mastering Fill Only Parts in Molding
newEvidence.scope: Directly discusses establishing fill-only parts, the limits of part-weight interpretation and the need to account for compressibility and gate state. Used to support the existence/purpose of a controlled fill-only study, not a universal fill percentage.

newEvidence.title: Seeing Gate Discharge with Sensors
newEvidence.scope: Describes a gate-seal study using part weight at different hold times and an alternative cavity-pressure-curve method; explicitly notes measurement and mould-behaviour limitations.

newEvidence.title: EMI Hot Runner Service Manual v2.4
newEvidence.scope: For purge/start-up activity, directs users to the injection-machine manufacturer's documentation and includes system-specific operating/safety instructions. Supports the Book boundary that purging and hot machine intervention cannot be governed by generic troubleshooting text.

newEvidence.title: Thin wall injection molding machine for plastic parts
newEvidence.scope: ENGEL explicitly links thin-wall filling capability to rapid acceleration, injection speed and available injection pressure, demonstrating that machine dynamics/capability matter beyond a nominal pressure number. Product-specific numeric performance is not imported as a Book setpoint.

newEvidence.title: Machine Independent Variables white paper
newEvidence.scope: Requires machine capability to cover acceptable shot capacity, melt preparation, volumetric injection rate and non-pressure-limited operation when transferring a process between machines. Used as corroborating capability evidence, not as a universal suitability percentage.

resolutions.reason: Independent in-mould sensing evidence distinguishes local cavity pressure from upstream machine signals, while process guidance shows that material resistance and pressure limitation alter machine pressure/velocity response. The claim remains diagnostic and non-unique.

Machine manufacturers treat screw position and cushion as monitored process values, but implementation and interpretation are controller/machine specific. The Book correctly avoids a universal cushion target.

RJG directly states that a pressure-limited fill may no longer maintain constant velocity when resistance increases. The Book wording preserves the distinction between the commanded control mode and a limiting condition and leaves controller-specific behavior external.

DME demonstrates that vent selection, location, geometry and installation are application/product specific. The requirement for tooling/site authorization is retained as a MouldMaster governance boundary rather than presented as a universal technical standard. No generic vent dimension is authorized.

Kistler distinguishes the temperature-control system from temperature measured in the mould and uses in-mould sensing to detect flow/heat-transfer problems. Exact offsets and sensor locations remain tool-specific.

Manufacturer monitoring guidance and measurement-system principles support diagnosing cooling with measured thermal/process evidence rather than inferring performance from a controller setpoint. Safe measurement methods remain site/tool specific as already excluded by the claim.

RJG directly documents fill-only process development and separately lists fill-only short-shot studies in its governed training. The Book claim describes purpose only and does not prescribe a universal fill percentage.

RJG directly describes varying hold time and weighing parts for a gate-seal study, while peer-reviewed in-mould sensor work independently supports gate-freeze interpretation from pressure/mass response. The claim explicitly treats a plateau as evidence rather than universal proof.

Manufacturer service material directs purge activity back to machine-specific documentation and the existing high-risk safety evidence requires hazardous-energy controls for service/mould-area intervention. The Book intentionally provides no purge or disassembly procedure.

ENGEL explicitly links thin-wall capability to acceleration, injection speed and pressure, while the consortium transfer framework independently requires sufficient shot capacity, volumetric injection rate and non-pressure-limited operation. This supports the multi-capability wording without importing product-specific numeric values.

publicationBoundary.reason: Clearing claim-level evidence holds is necessary but does not self-authorize publication. The Book accuracy gate still requires explicit chapter-level technical/publication sign-off, source-currentness confirmation at promotion, and release validation that read/listen surfaces render the same governed text.
